title: A local filtered colimit of etale algebras over a normal domain is a normal domain
statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain which is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ the localization $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain (a domain integrally closed in its field of fractions). Let $C$ be an $A$-algebra which is the colimit $C=\varinjlim_{i\in I}B_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of a filtered diagram $i\mapsto B_i$ of $A$-algebras such that each $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and suppose that $C$ is a local ring. Then:

(a) $C$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions);

(b) the structure map $A\to C$ is injective: every nonzero $a\in A$ has nonzero image in $C$.

(This applies to the strict henselization $C=(A_{\mathfrak p})^{sh}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], which is such a colimit and local; it is the implication 'R normal domain $\Rightarrow$ $R^{sh}$ normal domain' of Stacks 06DI, in the colimit form its proof uses.)

source.place: Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma (Tag 06DI, label more-algebra-lemma-henselization-normal), proof of 'R normal => R^sh normal': R^sh is a filtered colimit of etale (hence smooth) R-algebras; Algebra, Lemma (Tag 033C, normal goes up along smooth maps) and Lemma (Tag 037D, a directed colimit of normal rings is normal); a local normal ring is a normal domain (Algebra, Definition Tag 00GV and the remark after it). For (b): etale ring maps are flat (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U2 / 08WD), so a nonzero a, a nonzerodivisor of A, acts injectively on each B_i, hence on the filtered colimit C, and C is nonzero, being local.

proof.text: *The colimit as a colimit of rings.* Write $\iota_i:B_i\to C$ for the coprojections; they are $A$-algebra maps, and $I$ is filtered, in particular nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1), $(C,(\iota_i))$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram $i\mapsto B_i$ of commutative rings (with the same transition maps $B(\phi):B_i\to B_j$, which are $A$-algebra maps).

proof.text: *Each $B_i$ is a normal ring.* $A$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] by hypothesis and $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, so $B_i$ is a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal] (Stacks: etale hence smooth, and normality goes up along smooth ring maps, Algebra Lemma 033C).

proof.text: *$C$ is a normal ring.* By step 1, $C$ is the colimit of the filtered diagram of commutative rings $i\mapsto B_i$, each of which is a normal ring by step 2; hence $C$ is a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] (Stacks Algebra Lemma 037D; no condition on the transition maps is needed).

source.place: Lemma Tag 06DI (lemma-henselization-normal), proof of R normal => R^sh normal, citing Algebra Lemma 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring)

proof.text: *Proof of (a): a local normal ring is a normal domain.* Let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of the local ring $C$; it is prime. Every $s\in C\setminus\mathfrak m$ is a unit of $C$, so the localization map $C\to C_{\mathfrak m}$, $c\mapsto c/1$, is an isomorphism of rings: it is injective ($c/1=0$ means $sc=0$ for some unit $s$, so $c=0$) and surjective ($c/s=(cs^{-1})/1$). By step 3 and the definition of a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $C_{\mathfrak m}$ is a normal domain; a ring isomorphism carries a domain to a domain and extends to an isomorphism of the fields of fractions compatible with the inclusions, under which monic equations and their roots correspond, so $C$ is a normal domain. (Stacks, proof of 06DI: 'a local ring is normal if and only if it is a normal domain'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 06DI (lemma-henselization-normal), proof of R normal => R^sh normal (the preliminary remark) and Algebra Definition Tag 00GV

proof.text: *Nonzero elements of $A$ act injectively on each $B_i$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], $B_i$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $a\in A$, $a\ne0$. As $A$ is a domain, $\mu_a:A\to A$, $x\mapsto ax$, is an injective $A$-linear map; by flatness $\mu_a\otimes\mathrm{id}:A\otimes_AB_i\to A\otimes_AB_i$ is injective, and under the isomorphism $A\otimes_AB_i\cong B_i$, $x\otimes b\mapsto xb$, it is the map $b\mapsto ab$. So $b\mapsto ab$ is injective on $B_i$, for every $i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale) (6): etale ring maps are flat; Definition Tag 00HB (definition-flat). The argument for (b) is written by an agent: Stacks uses it implicitly in Etale Cohomology, Lemma 09Z5, where Spec K x_X Spec O^sh is the generic fibre

proof.text: *Proof of (b).* Let $a\in A$, $a\neq0$, and fix an object $i$ of $I$. Since $\iota_i$ is an $A$-algebra map, the image of $a$ in $C$ is $\iota_i(a\cdot1_{B_i})$. Suppose it is $0=\iota_i(0)$. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] there is a morphism $f:i\to k$ with $B(f)(a\cdot1_{B_i})=0$; as $B(f)$ is an $A$-algebra map, $a\cdot1_{B_k}=0$. Then $ab=(a\cdot1_{B_k})b=0$ for every $b\in B_k$, so by step 4 every $b\in B_k$ is $0$: $B_k=0$, i.e. $1_{B_k}=0$. Hence $1_C=\iota_k(1_{B_k})=\iota_k(0)=0$ and $C$ is the zero ring, which is not local (a local ring has a maximal ideal, a proper ideal, so $1\neq0$). This contradiction shows that the image of $a$ in $C$ is nonzero, i.e. $A\to C$ is injective.

Steps: (1) the A-algebra colimit is a ring colimit (existing elementwise node); (2) each B_i normal (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal, 033C + 00U9 + 02GJ); (3) C normal (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring, 037D + Categories 0032 for filtered vs directed); (4) a local normal ring is a normal domain (elementary from the new definition node def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, Mathlib leaf as a conjunction); (5)-(6) injectivity of A -> C: flatness of etale algebras (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat: Spec_iff + etale_algebraMap + Etale=>Smooth instance + Algebra.Smooth.flat) makes a nonzero a act injectively on each B_i, and if a died in C it would die at a stage B_k (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero), forcing B_k = 0 and C = 0, impossible for a local ring. The brief's suggestion that A -> B_i is injective for every i is false when B_i = 0 (the zero algebra is etale); the proof uses that C is nonzero instead.
